lyrics:
[Intro: solo piano hook, soft pad]

[Chorus: high male tenor, piano only]
Save me a seat
Wherever you've gone
I've been keeping notes
It won't be long
There's so much to go over
Since you got up to leave
So save me a seat

[Verse 1: male rap, warm and steady, soft beat enters]
Your number's in my phone and I haven't got the nerve
Still pass your exit, still slow down on the curve
Your laugh's in every room I ever shared with you
I keep on turning round to tell you something new
We were kids with one bike and a single pair of skates
Shared a locker, shared a lunch, shared a couple bad mistakes
You stood up at my wedding, I stood up at your door
I didn't know that standing was the thing we'd both be for

[Chorus: high male tenor, drums and strings]
Save me a seat
Wherever you've gone
I've been keeping notes
It won't be long
There's so much to go over
Since you got up to leave
So save me a seat

[Verse 2: male rap, lighter, a smile in it]
The team is still terrible, your mother's doing fine
Your kid has got your stubbornness and I have given mine
The keys to your old pickup, he's driving it too fast
I told him all the stories and I told him they were facts
I'm not big on praying but I'm talking to the sky
Mostly it's the scores and what I should have said, and why
Every road we ever took, I'm taking it for two
And every time I'm laughing there's a part of it that's you

[Bridge: sung, wordless, choir and piano, building]
Oh, oh-oh
Oh, oh-oh
Hold it for me
Hold it for me

[Final Chorus: tenor and choir, full band, held high note]
Save me a seat
Wherever you've gone
I've been keeping notes
It won't be long
There's so much to go over
Since you got up to leave
So save me a seat

[Outro: piano hook alone, last note held]
Save me a seat
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 80 BPM, 4/4, B-flat major. Slow, open and warm. A hymn with a heartbeat.

VOICE: A male tenor with a clean, high, boyish tone who sings the chorus softly, almost in falsetto, with a held high note at the end. A male rapper with a relaxed, warm, slightly raspy voice who delivers the verses like a conversation at a graveside or a bar. A small choir on the bridge and final chorus.

INSTRUMENTS: A simple, memorable piano figure that opens the song and runs under every chorus. A soft, steady hip-hop beat with a deep kick and finger snaps. Warm bass. A string section. A choir. Gentle electric guitar notes in the second verse.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, piano. 0:12 Chorus, voice and piano only. 0:42 Verse 1, the beat enters. 1:18 Chorus 2, with drums and strings. 1:48 Verse 2. 2:24 Bridge, wordless, with the choir building. 2:48 Final chorus with choir and a held high note. 3:24 Outro, the piano figure alone and one sung line at 3:40.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Mid-2010s film-soundtrack pop-rap: clean, wide and emotional, piano and voice exposed at the start, everything swelling by the end.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The opening chorus, sung over the piano alone before any beat arrives.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The friendship is decades long, and verse 2 is an update on a son, a mother and an old truck. The narrator has reached the age where this song stops being about a film.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Grief, memory, humour, a promise.
